text:
Source of MAGA Lies About Dr. Anthony Fauci
I have just learned where MAGA is acquiring its copious bullshit about Dr. Anthony Fauci. Lies like: “The text of authentic e-mails released by the DNI shows without a doubt that Fauci discussed the origins of the novel coronavirus with intelligence agencies. When he denied having done so, under oath, he committed perjury.”
Well, no. The public record shows Dr. Fauci explicitly stated under oath, “After the investigations began about COVID, I was briefed by intelligence agencies about possibilities of there being activities going on in different laboratories.”
The source of all the bullshit is RFK’s book, “The Real Anthony Fauci.”
Background on the author: RFK has no experience or academic training in medicine. He is a heroine junky, a bat-shit-crazy crackpot, an anti-vaxxer, a dumper of dead bears in Central Park, a self-alleged victim of a “brain-eating worm,” an assassin of science and, of course, Trump’s pick for Secretary of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
RFK abruptly dismissed all 17 medical experts on the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) -- the independent panel that advises the CDC on vaccine guidelines -- and then replaced them with fellow crackpots. Medical groups, including the California Medical Association, denounced RFK’s move as “reckless” and “anti-science,” pointing out most of the new appointees had no published literature on vaccine science or relevant clinical experience.
Additionally, RFK has replaced evidence-based data with political ideology by banning standard medical associations (such as the American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Medical Association) from ACIP workgroups.
RFK’s anti-vaccine superstitions degrade public trust in essential life-saving treatments, leading directly to dropping immunization rates and localized resurgences of preventable diseases like measles. In 2019, RFK went to Samoa and imbued government officials (including the prime minister) with his crackpot notion that measles vaccine causes measles. As a result, Samoa curtailed measles vaccinations, and 12 children died of measles.
RFK ordered the CDC to halt recommendations of COVID-19 vaccines for pregnant women and healthy children. He froze federal research funding into mRNA vaccine technology. He promoted unpasteurized raw milk despite known bacterial health risks.
RFK issued a demanding, public letter to the medical journal Toxicology Reports after its editors retracted a heavily flawed study that had claimed a causal link between vaccines and Sudden Infant Death Syndrome. RFK abused his federal power to intimidate a private publisher and influence independent peer-review processes to favor his personal notions.
RFK is pushing to eliminate public commentary requirements for major HHS policy decisions. Under the Administrative Procedures Act, federal health agencies traditionally must allow patients, healthcare providers, and advocacy groups to weigh in on proposed regulations. RFK wants to make his crackpot decisions “behind closed doors,” entirely stripping away democratic accountability.
On top of all that, RFK is a racist. He has publicly claimed that Black people should have a separate vaccine schedule based on his crackpot assumptions about their immune systems, as well as his 2023 conspiracy theory that COVID-19 was a genetically targeted bioweapon designed to spare certain ethnic groups while targeting Black and Caucasian populations.
********
Moving on to a brief review of RFK’s “The Real Anthony Fauci.” This book should not be discarded lightly. It should be hurled with great force (apologies to Dorothy Parker). It is a work of fiction, a slovenly one at that. Its central thesis is that Dr. Fauci and a nameless “vaccine cartel” intentionally suppressed cheap, effective treatments to pave the way for emergency vaccine profits.
RFK wrongly claims that quack drugs like hydroxychloroquine and ivermectin (promoted by Trump along with bleach) are highly effective against COVID-19, and that public health officials deliberately rigged or ignored studies to make them look ineffective.
Broad global scientific consensus—backed by large-scale, randomized, double-blind clinical trials—concluded that neither hydroxychloroquine nor ivermectin provides the slightest benefit against COVID-19. RFK’s allegations rely on cherry-picked data, low-quality observational studies, and an elaborate conspiracy narrative that ignores the transparent, peer-reviewed global effort to find viable treatments.
RFK wrongly portrayed Dr. Fauci as the ultimate architect of a global conspiracy. RFK vastly exaggerated his actual administrative power. RFK wrongly frames Dr. Fauci as wielding unparalleled power over global democracy, dictating American medical choices almost single-handedly.
Public health experts note that while Dr. Fauci was an advisor, policy decisions—such as lockdowns, mask mandates, and approvals—were fragmented across state governors, independent regulatory committees at the FDA, the CDC, and various international bodies, none of which Dr. Fauci controlled.
RFK echoes long-debunked conspiracy theories from early HIV denialists, suggesting that HIV is not the sole or true cause of AIDS and claiming that the virus particle has never been properly isolated. The link between HIV and AIDS is one of the most thoroughly investigated and proven realities in modern medicine. By breathing life back into decades-old denialism, the book promotes a highly dangerous narrative that historically led people to refuse life-saving antiretroviral treatments.
RFK makes numerous false claims regarding the development, safety testing, and efficacy of COVID-19 and childhood vaccines. He wrongly asserts that vaccines are not safety-tested in clinical trials before being approved, and that Phase 1 trials for mRNA vaccines showed a “100% injury rate.” Fact-checkers call the claim that vaccines skip safety testing “overtly false,” noting that tens of thousands of participants take part in multi-phase clinical trials before public distribution.
Furthermore, the “100% injury rate” claim was flagged as a severe distortion of data. The data RFK referenced actually show that participants experienced typical, mild-to-moderate side effects (like temporary soreness at the injection site or mild chills), which Kennedy falsely equated with severe, lasting medical injuries.
The sources RFK used to build his crackpot claims are rife with systemic errors in how research was represented. Medical reviewers (such as physician Theodore Dalrymple and molecular biologist Dan Wilson) fact-checked specific scientific papers cited in the book’s footnotes. They found that RFK frequently inverted or fundamentally misunderstood the conclusions of the papers he cited, relying on an “illusion of fact” by presenting dense graphs and citations that actually contradicted his own written claims when read objectively.
Ultimately, medical experts view the book not as a credible piece of investigative journalism, but as an exercise in confirmation bias that uses flawed data to construct a dangerous anti-science narrative.

RFK issued a demanding, public letter to the medical journal Toxicology Reports after its editors retracted a heavily flawed study that had claimed a causal link between vaccines and Sudden Infant Death Syndrome.
